counterfactual_missing_items: No formal compartment pressure or urine myoglobin measurement is provided
No explicit statement of prolonged immobility or positional compression
No documented muscle weakness or tenderness beyond the right forearm/eyelid findings
decisive_items: pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of his right eyelids and forearm
tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and restricted motility in all fields of gaze
response.rationale: R4 best integrates the systemic evidence: the markedly elevated CK and creatinine, alcohol/opioid exposure, and right-sided eyelid/forearm induration point to rhabdomyolysis with compartment syndrome, which can produce the orbital compartment findings and secondary retinal ischemia. R3 captures the retinal arterial occlusion features but cannot account for the CK elevation, AKI, or forearm involvement and is a downstream complication rather than the unifying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Only drug exposure and vision loss are cited; toxic optic neuropathy does not explain orbital edema, retinal perfusion defects, CK elevation, or forearm findings.
Compressive optic neuropathy explains NLP/RAPD but not CK/AKI, forearm induration, or retinal arterial occlusion; it is a complication of the underlying process.
Acute angle-closure glaucoma fits corneal haze and elevated IOP/pupil, but not tense orbital edema, restricted motility, serous retinal detachment, delayed vascular filling, or rhabdomyolysis.
